theme: Crop retention, changing composition and source denominators after Harappan urban decline
question: Which parts of the Jognakhera crop-continuity claim survive an independent source audit, and what comparison data can support a regional test?
outcome: Audited the focal paper and extracted nine published phase summaries at five comparison sites. Bahola's winter share rises by 10.42 percentage points and its summer share falls by 15.36 points between Late Harappan and PGW assemblages. Reconstructed cereal-denominator millet figures of 54.05% and 71.37%. The focal paper's three reported crop date ranges predate a 1200 BCE PGW reference; its complete supplement and layer-phase joins remain uninspected. The news article misreads a modern crop list as archaeological finds. No regional significance test or new excavation claim is made.
challenge: Focal supplementary DOCX access failed; direct publisher access returned a JavaScript challenge and the author PDF download returned 403. Pooled phase percentages lack deposit-level uncertainty and common recovery denominators. Several comparison publications share one excavation lineage.
remedy: Preserved failed requests and source scope, reused an identical-hash Cambridge manuscript with supplement, inspected comparison tables visually, and checked the calculations through pdfplumber and exact rational arithmetic. All 52 same-contributor checks pass. Recorded missing fields and a prospective recovery-controlled design; retained run-v1 beside the reproducible-output naming repair in run-v2.
retry_when: The Jognakhera supplement, independently associated layer dates and PGW sample joins, or comparable deposit-level crop counts and recovery metadata at independent sites become available. New familiar phase-percentage contrasts alone do not establish unchanged management or drought causation.
